newsitem.title: USA: Presidential campaign debates at a glance.
newsitem.headline: Presidential campaign debates at a glance.

text.p: Here are the details of the three nationally televised 90-minute debates leading up to the Nov. 5 presidential elections, according to the bipartisan Commission on Presidential Debates.
All three debates will begin at 9 p.m. EDT (0100 GMT) running with no commercials, and all will be moderated by PBS anchor Jim Lehrer.

SUNDAY, OCTOBER 6: Democratic President Bill Clinton and Republican challenger Bob Dole will debate at the Bushnell Theatre in Hartford, Connecticut. The two debaters, standing behind podiums, have two minutes each for both opening and closing statements, with the order of speech to be decided by a coin toss. Whoever gives the first opening statement will deliver the second closing statement.

Questions selected by the moderator will be posed first to one candidate, who has 90 seconds to respond. Then the second candidate has 60 seconds to reply and the first candidate has an additional 30 seconds to answer the reply.
WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 9: Vice presidential candidates Al Gore and Jack Kemp will debate at Bayfront Centre in St. Petersburg, Florida, with podiums and one moderator. Same format as October 6 debate.

WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 16: Presidential candidates Dole and Clinton will debate at the University of California in San Diego. The debate will take place within a "town hall" format with questions from the audience. The audience will be selected by the Gallup polling organisation.
